polls.text: Do people agree that there is a problem to be solved?

chat.author: Emelia Smith
chat.text: Has anyone said anything yet? I'm not hearing audio?

chat.author: Rifaat Shekh-Yusef
chat.text: Yes

chat.author: Emelia Smith
chat.text: I'm not getting any audio at all..

chat.author: Rifaat Shekh-Yusef
chat.text: It seems that the problem is on your side

chat.author: Emelia Smith
chat.text: trying a different internet connection..

chat.author: Emelia Smith
chat.text: Finally got audio, was definitely my end, but was having connectiivty issues with zulip

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: do you need to refresh materials, maybe? I've had that happen

chat.author: Jeff Lombardo
chat.text: just happened to me

chat.author: Deb Cooley
chat.text: The wrong version is on the DT, so I suspect that the wrong version was uploaded.

chat.author: Deb Cooley
chat.text: no worries

chat.author: Emelia Smith
chat.text: I've been working on FedCM + OAuth which I think may provide an alternative, where FedCM takes the place of authorization + PAR, and instead it's the FedCM API call then a authorization code exchange to the token endpoint

chat.author: Emelia Smith
chat.text: Going to try to write a profile soon

chat.author: krooj
chat.text: Blowing up header buffers is a real concern and something we see regularly

chat.author: Maxwell Gerber
chat.text: What was the reason a generic HTTP proposal was rejected? Do other protocols have similar carveouts in HTTP/Browser semantics?

chat.author: Emelia Smith
chat.text: The one I've seen blow Location headers up has been the state parameter where apps are trying to be stateless and pack absolutely everything into the state parameter

chat.author: Aaron Parecki
chat.text: I can't go off mute right now but I'm generally on board with this pattern, seems like it addresses a lot of the security issues described in the browser apps BCP

chat.author: Jeff Lombardo
chat.text: or to face the downgrading attacks. If Code capture is problematic, then downgrade should not be possible

chat.author: Emelia Smith
chat.text: https://github.com/fedidcg/idp-initiated

chat.author: Aaron Parecki
chat.text: But it would be useful to go through the browser apps BCP which lists out a bunch of attacker models and see whether this actually solves those

chat.author: Emelia Smith
chat.text: I think everyone doing credentials and redirects ended up overloading oauth, no?

chat.author: Emelia Smith
chat.text: https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-hardt-oauth-protected-authorization-00.html#section-10.5

chat.author: Maxwell Gerber
chat.text: Can we name the header something non-OAuth specific even if the work was done in OAuth? I worry that another protocol/ecosystem would be forced to reuse the header if they want the same security properties

chat.author: Brian Campbell
chat.text: it does seem not quite right to try and define browser and http behavior here  (a corollary of sorts to Max's points/questions)

chat.author: Aaron Parecki
chat.text: I'm here just on an airplane sorry

chat.author: Maxwell Gerber
chat.text: https://datatracker.ietf.org/meeting/124/materials/slides-124-oauth-sessa-browser-swapping-01

chat.author: Maxwell Gerber
chat.text: ^ Covers PKCE and how it doesn't help this attack

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: notes from the HTTP meeting where this was previously presented: https://datatracker.ietf.org/meeting/125/materials/minutes-125-httpbis-00

chat.author: Aaron Parecki
chat.text: What I'm getting from this is that we realy need a crisp defintion of the attacks this would address

chat.author: Aaron Parecki
chat.text: This would be a significant implementation lift across the ecosystem, so it needs to be clear that it's worth doing. I do agree this particular mechanism is well defined for what it does.

chat.author: Emelia Smith
chat.text: Yeah, I think binding the PKCE code to the user-agent's metadata (ip, user-agent, etc) would solve the Browser-Swapping Attack

chat.author: Jeff Lombardo
chat.text: but the attack from Jonas is that the attack starts at the attacker so it controls the challenge and the verifier submission therefore it could solve the PKCE

chat.author: Jeff Lombardo
chat.text: the attack from Jonas is that it is too easy for the attack-ee to copy paste the code to the attacker

chat.author: Jeff Lombardo
chat.text: headers solve this part of the attack path

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: I feel like it's hard to say "a problem" when we are dancing around which problem/surface.

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: yeah +1 to Emilia

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: *Emelia

chat.author: Maxwell Gerber
chat.text: I'm operating under "Is the browser-swapping attack from 124 a problem to be solved"

chat.author: Jeff Lombardo
chat.text: Details of the attack from Jonas - https://blog.syss.com/posts/browser_swapping/

chat.author: Aaron Parecki
chat.text: IIRC the attack relies on the attacker convincing the user to copy and paste the authorization code in the url to the attacker manually

chat.author: Jeff Lombardo
chat.text: Eaxact

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: +1 Deb

chat.author: Emelia Smith
chat.text: +1 Deb

chat.author: Hannes Tschofenig
chat.text: I agree.

chat.author: Aaron Parecki
chat.text: +1 Deb, any doc defining a new mechanism needs to restate the problem. If we just spent an hour getting everyone to remember the presentation from 6 months ago seems like we could shortcut that with a better intro in the doc

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: esp when the presentation has a stack of attacks with different attacker models

chat.author: Emelia Smith
chat.text: Well, we can't say we want OAuth to adopt the work without the problem statements?

chat.author: Justin Richer
chat.text: we shouldn't adopt a solution and then work on the problem

chat.author: Emelia Smith
chat.text: I'd be inclined to put it right between section 2 & 3 there

chat.author: Emelia Smith
chat.text: I suspect many of these attacks could be mitigated by requiring PAR, such that the request_uri is tagged to the client instance that issued the PAR request, and then the /authorize endpoint would entirely dead-end the request without redirecting because the request_uri's metadata doesn't match the current requestor's metadata

chat.author: Emelia Smith
chat.text: (We have a protection like this in the AT Protocol OAuth code where we record user-agent and IP address agains the PAR request_uri such that we can't get confusion here
